criteria_assessments.Assessment_Finding: Qualified as a full-suite CCaaS core peer; rational class remains cloud-native / programmable because AWS-native architecture and operating ownership materially affect buyer fit.
criteria_assessments.Buyer_Fit_Notes: Compare primarily with programmable/cloud-native peers while still including it in full-suite enterprise shortlists.
criteria_assessments.Implementation_Change_Implication: Classification only.
criteria_assessments.Production_Operating_Risk: Low category-qualification risk.

criteria_assessments.Assessment_Finding: The historical builder-only thesis is stale: current Connect Customer is materially more packaged, but advanced value still rises with AWS/cloud operating maturity.
criteria_assessments.Buyer_Fit_Notes: Fit rises for organizations comfortable treating contact center as a governed cloud workload; it no longer requires a pure builder persona for common capabilities.
criteria_assessments.Implementation_Change_Implication: Buyer must decide how much native packaging vs AWS-native customization it intends to use.
criteria_assessments.Production_Operating_Risk: Oversimplifying it as either a toolkit or turnkey suite can misclassify fit.

criteria_assessments.Assessment_Finding: Global telephony/compliance reach is broad, but Global Resiliency pairings and some AI inference paths are Region-specific.
criteria_assessments.Buyer_Fit_Notes: Fit rises for supported global architectures and can fall sharply where exact residency/paired-Region requirements are non-negotiable.
criteria_assessments.Implementation_Change_Implication: Architecture must map instance Region, resilient pair, AI inference and downstream AWS services.
criteria_assessments.Production_Operating_Risk: Sovereignty or residency requirements can conflict with supported Region pairs or cross-region AI inference.

criteria_assessments.Assessment_Finding: Broad global telephony is documented, with 110+ countries for claimed numbers and 200+ outbound destinations.
criteria_assessments.Buyer_Fit_Notes: Strong fit for multinational voice when exact countries pass proof.
criteria_assessments.Implementation_Change_Implication: Country-by-country telecom design and porting remain SOW work.
criteria_assessments.Production_Operating_Risk: Country-specific number types, emergency services, porting, carrier routing and pricing still vary.

criteria_assessments.Assessment_Finding: Queues, routing profiles, proficiencies and programmable flows provide strong omnichannel routing, including shared-agent patterns.
criteria_assessments.Buyer_Fit_Notes: Fit rises for programmable routing and multi-skill operations; down where complex logic must remain business-admin-only.
criteria_assessments.Implementation_Change_Implication: Flow/routing design should use reusable patterns, testing and IaC where practical.
criteria_assessments.Production_Operating_Risk: Complex routing can become a software/configuration asset that requires engineering discipline.

criteria_assessments.Assessment_Finding: Voice, chat, email, tasks and digital messaging are native current channels with shared routing/workspace surfaces.
criteria_assessments.Buyer_Fit_Notes: Broad omnichannel fit is now stronger than older Amazon Connect positioning implied.
criteria_assessments.Implementation_Change_Implication: Channel onboarding, compliance, integration and failure testing remain scoped work.
criteria_assessments.Production_Operating_Risk: Critical-channel depth and provider-specific failure behavior remain channel-specific.

criteria_assessments.Assessment_Finding: Predictive, progressive and agentless voice outbound are current, with digital campaign options and usage-based attempt/channel economics.
criteria_assessments.Buyer_Fit_Notes: Fit rises for variable-volume proactive engagement when usage economics and regulation align.
criteria_assessments.Implementation_Change_Implication: Campaign rules, lists, identity, compliance and cost controls must be designed.
criteria_assessments.Production_Operating_Risk: Consent, abandonment, dialing regulations and attempt economics can become structural by geography/use case.

criteria_assessments.Assessment_Finding: Native WFM, adherence, capacity planning, human/self-service evaluations and GenAI-assisted quality are now materially deeper than the Phase 1 baseline.
criteria_assessments.Buyer_Fit_Notes: Current product fit rises materially for buyers wanting native WFM/QM rather than assembling AWS services themselves.
criteria_assessments.Implementation_Change_Implication: Historical data readiness, workforce rules and QA calibration are implementation work.
criteria_assessments.Production_Operating_Risk: Buyer-specific forecasting accuracy, scheduling constraints and evaluation validity are not proven by feature breadth.

criteria_assessments.Assessment_Finding: Native conversational analytics now spans voice, chat and email; historical data lake and real-time streaming serve different latency needs.
criteria_assessments.Buyer_Fit_Notes: Fit rises for buyers wanting native analytics plus open AWS data paths.
criteria_assessments.Implementation_Change_Implication: Architecture must separate native dashboards, data lake and streaming use cases.
criteria_assessments.Production_Operating_Risk: Using the wrong analytics path can create freshness gaps or unnecessary AWS complexity.

criteria_assessments.Assessment_Finding: Current agent workspace integrates contact controls, apps, AI, tasks, Cases and Profiles; supervisor/manager surfaces continue to evolve.
criteria_assessments.Buyer_Fit_Notes: Fit rises for buyers wanting native workspace plus extension capability.
criteria_assessments.Implementation_Change_Implication: Workspace configuration and external-app lifecycle need testing.
criteria_assessments.Production_Operating_Risk: Custom applications and complex workflows can still create desktop fragmentation; manager AI is preview.

criteria_assessments.Assessment_Finding: Broad public APIs expose core routing, users, metrics, resiliency and resource administration.
criteria_assessments.Buyer_Fit_Notes: Strong fit for API-driven enterprises; less attractive if deep customization is expected without engineering ownership.
criteria_assessments.Implementation_Change_Implication: Technical teams must own auth, deployment, limits, regression and observability for custom integrations.
criteria_assessments.Production_Operating_Risk: API quotas and custom implementation ownership become production concerns at scale.

criteria_assessments.Assessment_Finding: Data access is strong through Kinesis, APIs, data lake and customer-controlled AWS storage; native data-lake freshness is under an hour rather than real time.
criteria_assessments.Buyer_Fit_Notes: Fit rises for data-lake/streaming buyers; strategic coupling rises with custom AWS pipelines.
criteria_assessments.Implementation_Change_Implication: Data architecture must choose the right freshness path and retention destination.
criteria_assessments.Production_Operating_Risk: AWS-native pipelines can add IAM, streaming, storage, schema and cost complexity.

criteria_assessments.Assessment_Finding: Regional service commitment is 99.99%; paired-Region Global Resiliency now supports active-active patterns but only across defined Region pairs.
criteria_assessments.Buyer_Fit_Notes: Fit is strong when supported Region pairs meet requirements; structural risk appears when they do not.
criteria_assessments.Implementation_Change_Implication: Multi-region design, dependency replication and failover tests are material implementation work.
criteria_assessments.Production_Operating_Risk: End-to-end resilience can fail outside the Connect SLA through unsupported Region topology, telecom, Lambda, CRM, streams or other dependencies.

criteria_assessments.Assessment_Finding: Amazon Connect is in current FedRAMP and PCI scopes, while AWS guidance makes the customer's end-to-end shared-responsibility obligations explicit.
criteria_assessments.Buyer_Fit_Notes: Fit rises for regulated AWS buyers with mature shared-responsibility governance.
criteria_assessments.Implementation_Change_Implication: Security architecture must include every connected AWS and third-party service.
criteria_assessments.Production_Operating_Risk: A compliant Connect service does not make Lambda, CRM, storage, AI or other dependencies compliant by default.

criteria_assessments.Assessment_Finding: Real-time AI assistance is GA and action-capable; manager assistance remains preview and is excluded from production credit.
criteria_assessments.Buyer_Fit_Notes: Strong fit for native AI assist where buyer accepts governed AI operations.
criteria_assessments.Implementation_Change_Implication: Knowledge, prompts, permissions and evaluation suites require ongoing ownership.
criteria_assessments.Production_Operating_Risk: Assist quality, timing and action safety remain production proof items.

criteria_assessments.Assessment_Finding: Generative AI is embedded in summaries, evaluations, prompts and agent/self-service experiences.

criteria_assessments.Implementation_Change_Implication: Evaluation sets and prompt/model version controls are required.
criteria_assessments.Production_Operating_Risk: Generation quality and model behavior vary by workflow and selected/managed model.

criteria_assessments.Assessment_Finding: Native AI and flows automate recommendations, evaluations, customer interactions and multi-step processes.
criteria_assessments.Buyer_Fit_Notes: Strong fit for governed automation with AWS-native workflow ownership.
criteria_assessments.Implementation_Change_Implication: Exception paths, test cases and rollback/fallback need explicit design.
criteria_assessments.Production_Operating_Risk: Automation can amplify bad rules, stale knowledge or integration failures.

criteria_assessments.Assessment_Finding: AI agents can invoke tools and take backend actions with security-profile controls.

criteria_assessments.Implementation_Change_Implication: High-consequence actions require idempotency, validation, audit and compensation design in the underlying tool/integration.
criteria_assessments.Production_Operating_Risk: Permission controls do not by themselves prevent duplicate, stale-state or partially successful transactions.

criteria_assessments.Assessment_Finding: Connect supports multi-step agentic orchestration and A2A collaboration with external agents.
criteria_assessments.Buyer_Fit_Notes: Moves up for multi-agent automation buyers; proof burden rises with external agents.
criteria_assessments.Implementation_Change_Implication: Tracing, identity, tool contracts, fallback and end-to-end evaluation must be engineered.
criteria_assessments.Production_Operating_Risk: Cross-agent/tool dependencies broaden the incident and governance boundary.

criteria_assessments.Assessment_Finding: Many custom prompts allow supported Bedrock model selection and pinning, while other managed features can change underlying models and use cross-region inference.
criteria_assessments.Buyer_Fit_Notes: Fit rises for use cases that can use selectable prompts; fit can fall under strict model/in-region constraints.
criteria_assessments.Implementation_Change_Implication: Buyer must inventory pinned vs managed models and inference Regions by workflow.
criteria_assessments.Production_Operating_Risk: Model governance is not uniform across all AI features; sovereignty and regression obligations can differ by mode.

criteria_assessments.Assessment_Finding: AI agents can use configured knowledge and prompt context for assistance/self-service, with guardrail controls applied by workflow.
criteria_assessments.Buyer_Fit_Notes: Fit rises for buyers wanting native grounded AI and willing to govern enterprise knowledge.
criteria_assessments.Implementation_Change_Implication: Knowledge onboarding, evaluation and content lifecycle are persistent run-state work.
criteria_assessments.Production_Operating_Risk: Retrieval quality, stale/conflicting content, provenance and knowledge ownership remain buyer responsibilities.

criteria_assessments.Assessment_Finding: Concrete controls exist for permissions, guardrails, model selection/pinning and documented Bedrock data-use posture, but control coverage differs by agent type.
criteria_assessments.Buyer_Fit_Notes: Fit is strong for controlled AI when workflow-specific gaps are acceptable or mitigated.
criteria_assessments.Implementation_Change_Implication: Governance must map controls to each agent/prompt/tool rather than rely on a single platform policy.
criteria_assessments.Production_Operating_Risk: Orchestration agents currently lack contextual-grounding guardrail support, creating a workflow-specific control gap.

criteria_assessments.Assessment_Finding: Connect Customer bundles significant AI in channel pricing, while some AI/tooling can still invoke separately priced AWS services such as Bedrock, AgentCore, Lambda or related data services.
criteria_assessments.Buyer_Fit_Notes: Fit rises where AWS FinOps is mature; predictability falls if AI service dependencies are not modeled.
criteria_assessments.Implementation_Change_Implication: TCO must meter AI calls, tools, downstream services and testing separately where applicable.
criteria_assessments.Production_Operating_Risk: Agentic expansion can shift cost from CCaaS feature fees into broader AWS consumption.

criteria_assessments.Assessment_Finding: The platform provides native AI agents, prompts, guardrails and testing surfaces, but production operability still depends on knowledge, tools, IAM, observability, evaluations and model lifecycle.
criteria_assessments.Buyer_Fit_Notes: Moves up for mature AWS/AI operations; down where AI is expected to require no ongoing ownership.
criteria_assessments.Implementation_Change_Implication: AI implementation must include evaluation, regression, permissions, cost and incident runbooks.
criteria_assessments.Production_Operating_Risk: Demo-ready AI can become operationally fragile without AI Ops ownership.

criteria_assessments.Assessment_Finding: Managed integration paths exist for major CRMs and Connect Health provides a direct Epic path for healthcare.
criteria_assessments.Buyer_Fit_Notes: Fit rises when the buyer's systems align with documented integrations and AWS architecture.
criteria_assessments.Implementation_Change_Implication: Critical systems require workflow-level proof and incident RACI.
criteria_assessments.Production_Operating_Risk: Integration depth and surrounding AWS services differ by target system.

criteria_assessments.Production_Operating_Risk: Depth comes with architecture choices and can shift ownership to cloud engineering.

criteria_assessments.Buyer_Fit_Notes: Fit depends on operational maturity and clear multi-party RACI.
criteria_assessments.Implementation_Change_Implication: SOW/contract must assign first response, log ownership and escalation by dependency.
criteria_assessments.Production_Operating_Risk: Cross-service support boundaries can extend MTTR during partial failures.

criteria_assessments.Buyer_Fit_Notes: No negative capability inference; observability must be proven on the actual architecture.
criteria_assessments.Implementation_Change_Implication: Buyer must instrument end-to-end transactions and test degraded modes.
criteria_assessments.Production_Operating_Risk: Partial success or silent dependency failure can become customer-impacting behavior.

criteria_assessments.Buyer_Fit_Notes: Moves up for builder-capable teams; down for buyers expecting deep customization with minimal technical bench.
criteria_assessments.Implementation_Change_Implication: Use native packaged capability first, then explicit engineering ownership for extensions.
criteria_assessments.Production_Operating_Risk: Custom architecture can become expensive to build, test and maintain.

criteria_assessments.Implementation_Change_Implication: Discovery must scope AWS dependencies, IAM, quotas, telephony, flows, data, AI, resilience and operating ownership.
criteria_assessments.Production_Operating_Risk: The primary risk is architecture/operating complexity rather than lack of capability.

criteria_assessments.Assessment_Finding: Discovery burden rises with Region topology, telephony, quota sizing, IAM, integrations, data streaming, AI tooling, support tier and IaC decisions.

criteria_assessments.Implementation_Change_Implication: Enterprise architecture should freeze these dependencies before detailed SOW.
criteria_assessments.Production_Operating_Risk: Architecture omissions can surface only at scale or during failover.

criteria_assessments.Assessment_Finding: AWS publishes repeatable migration patterns and offers scalable infrastructure, but complex source routing, numbers, recordings, integrations and operating processes still require transformation work.
criteria_assessments.Buyer_Fit_Notes: Fit improves where buyer accepts programmatic migration and engineering upfront investment.
criteria_assessments.Implementation_Change_Implication: Migration waves, parity mapping, number/data handling and acceptance criteria must be explicit.
criteria_assessments.Production_Operating_Risk: A rapid migration can recreate legacy logic badly or hit quotas/dependency gaps.

criteria_assessments.Assessment_Finding: Native voice/chat interaction simulation with expected outcomes and logs materially improves pre-production testing, but it does not replace full integration/cutover UAT.
criteria_assessments.Buyer_Fit_Notes: Fit rises for high-change teams that operationalize automated regression.
criteria_assessments.Implementation_Change_Implication: UAT must layer native simulation with end-to-end dependency and cutover tests.
criteria_assessments.Production_Operating_Risk: False confidence can arise if only flow logic is tested while CRM, telecom or backend tools are omitted.

criteria_assessments.Assessment_Finding: SOW exposure is concentrated in telephony, AWS service dependencies, IAM, quota sizing, flows, CRM/serverless integration, data, AI, multi-region resilience and support responsibilities.
criteria_assessments.Buyer_Fit_Notes: Fit falls when procurement expects a single opaque implementation bundle without architecture responsibility.
criteria_assessments.Implementation_Change_Implication: Workstream-level responsibilities and acceptance criteria are mandatory.
criteria_assessments.Production_Operating_Risk: Undefined dependency ownership can become change-order and production risk.

criteria_assessments.Assessment_Finding: AWS provides migration patterns and the broader AWS partner/services ecosystem can support complex deployments, but delivery quality depends heavily on the named team and architecture.
criteria_assessments.Buyer_Fit_Notes: Fit rises when partner and buyer both have AWS + CX operating credibility.
criteria_assessments.Implementation_Change_Implication: Buyer should validate the actual solution architect/SI team and comparable references.
criteria_assessments.Production_Operating_Risk: A generic AWS partner credential does not guarantee contact-center implementation depth.

criteria_assessments.Assessment_Finding: Day-2 ownership extends beyond contact-center administration into AWS Support, quotas, IAM, telemetry, costs and any customer-managed integrations/data services.
criteria_assessments.Buyer_Fit_Notes: Moves down when buyer wants a no-cloud-operations contact-center operating model.
criteria_assessments.Implementation_Change_Implication: Named platform owners and AWS account governance are required for advanced deployments.
criteria_assessments.Production_Operating_Risk: Understaffed CloudOps can turn adjustable quotas or external-service failures into customer-facing incidents.

criteria_assessments.Assessment_Finding: Routine queues/routing/flows can be administered natively; programmatic resource management supports stronger change control for complex environments.
criteria_assessments.Buyer_Fit_Notes: Strong fit where platform engineering complements contact-center administration.
criteria_assessments.Implementation_Change_Implication: Ownership should separate routine contact-center configuration from engineered extensions.
criteria_assessments.Production_Operating_Risk: Complex flows and Lambda-backed logic can exceed business-admin skill levels.

criteria_assessments.Assessment_Finding: Native WFM, evaluations and analytics provide buyer-admin surfaces; advanced use still requires data/rules/calibration expertise.
criteria_assessments.Buyer_Fit_Notes: Fit is materially stronger than Phase 1 implied for native workforce/quality operations.
criteria_assessments.Implementation_Change_Implication: Admins need role-specific governance and regression/calibration processes.
criteria_assessments.Production_Operating_Risk: Operational teams can misconfigure forecasts, evaluations or analytics despite native tooling.

criteria_assessments.Assessment_Finding: Integration, workflow and AI changes can be highly automatable, but advanced work often requires cloud engineers/AI Ops and may span multiple AWS services.
criteria_assessments.Buyer_Fit_Notes: Moves down if complex change must remain within a small business-admin team.
criteria_assessments.Implementation_Change_Implication: RACI and automated testing/promotion should be designed at build time.
criteria_assessments.Production_Operating_Risk: Change ownership can fragment across contact-center admin, cloud engineering, data, AI and application teams.

criteria_assessments.Assessment_Finding: CloudFormation, flow resources and interaction simulation create a strong change-management foundation, but full resource parity is not uniform and the Instance resource remains preview.
criteria_assessments.Buyer_Fit_Notes: Strong fit for DevOps buyers after resource-level validation.
criteria_assessments.Implementation_Change_Implication: Buyer should prove dev/test/prod, versioning, drift detection, rollback and resource parity.
criteria_assessments.Production_Operating_Risk: Assuming complete IaC coverage can create unmanaged drift for unsupported/preview resources.

criteria_assessments.Assessment_Finding: CloudWatch/quota monitoring, AWS support and test diagnostics provide strong observability building blocks; end-to-end incidents still cross service boundaries.
criteria_assessments.Buyer_Fit_Notes: Moves up with mature CloudOps; down when monitoring is expected to be vendor-operated by default.
criteria_assessments.Implementation_Change_Implication: Production runbooks need quota dashboards, dependency health, logs and support escalation.
criteria_assessments.Production_Operating_Risk: Quotas, external systems and serverless dependencies can create failure outside the core SLA.

criteria_assessments.Assessment_Finding: The platform does not structurally require AWS Professional Services, but complex estates can depend heavily on SI/cloud engineering capacity.
criteria_assessments.Buyer_Fit_Notes: Fit rises where buyer can own or source AWS engineering competitively.
criteria_assessments.Implementation_Change_Implication: SOW should identify custom assets and who can maintain them without the original SI.
criteria_assessments.Production_Operating_Risk: Dependency risk shifts from vendor PS lock-in toward customer/SI engineering capability.

criteria_assessments.Assessment_Finding: Public pricing is granular usage-based and bundles more current capability than Phase 1 assumed; total platform cost still spans channels, telecom, outbound, adjunct AWS services and support.
criteria_assessments.Buyer_Fit_Notes: Strong fit where consumption aligns with demand and FinOps is mature.
criteria_assessments.Implementation_Change_Implication: Build workload-based TCO rather than per-seat comparisons.
criteria_assessments.Production_Operating_Risk: Unit-level simplicity can hide aggregate workload/service costs.

criteria_assessments.Assessment_Finding: Transformation cost is dominated by architecture, migration, integrations, IAM, data, resilience, AI and test automation rather than license activation.
criteria_assessments.Buyer_Fit_Notes: Fit depends on whether customization value justifies transformation investment.
criteria_assessments.Implementation_Change_Implication: Model customer/SI/cloud engineering and migration as a separate TCO layer.
criteria_assessments.Production_Operating_Risk: Engineering labor can exceed software cost in a heavily customized deployment.

criteria_assessments.Assessment_Finding: Run-state cost includes AWS Support plus CloudOps/FinOps, admin, integration/data operations and AI evaluation/maintenance where used.
criteria_assessments.Buyer_Fit_Notes: Moves up when these capabilities are shared across a mature AWS operating model.
criteria_assessments.Implementation_Change_Implication: Allocate support and internal labor to the contact-center workload explicitly.
criteria_assessments.Production_Operating_Risk: Ongoing cloud engineering and support spend can be omitted from CCaaS-only business cases.

criteria_assessments.Assessment_Finding: Usage pricing is naturally elastic, but telephony, outbound attempts, AI/tool calls and surrounding AWS services can create nonlinear demand sensitivity.
criteria_assessments.Buyer_Fit_Notes: Fit rises where variable demand is well instrumented.
criteria_assessments.Implementation_Change_Implication: Low/base/high scenarios and AWS Budgets/cost monitoring are required.
criteria_assessments.Production_Operating_Risk: Seasonal bursts can be economically efficient or unexpectedly expensive depending workload composition.

criteria_assessments.Assessment_Finding: Public Connect Customer pricing states no minimums or long-term contracts, giving strong baseline elasticity; private enterprise discount/commitment structures remain buyer-specific.
criteria_assessments.Buyer_Fit_Notes: Public model fits buyers valuing flexibility; contract-specific protections still require review.
criteria_assessments.Implementation_Change_Implication: Procurement must compare pure on-demand and committed-discount structures.
criteria_assessments.Production_Operating_Risk: Negotiated discount programs can reintroduce commitment risk not visible on public pricing.

criteria_assessments.Assessment_Finding: Tag-based controls support segmentation for many resources, but current gaps exist across agent queues, scheduled reports and some analytics surfaces.
criteria_assessments.Buyer_Fit_Notes: Potentially strong but not universally proven for strict client-isolation models.
criteria_assessments.Implementation_Change_Implication: POC must prove client isolation across routing, profiles, recordings, analytics and integrations or justify separate instances.
criteria_assessments.Production_Operating_Risk: A shared-instance BPO design may not provide hard isolation on every required surface.

criteria_assessments.Assessment_Finding: AWS explicitly documents a shared-agent two-client BPO pattern; current Customer pricing is not seat-based, but exact client/license allocation is not a packaged BPO construct.
criteria_assessments.Buyer_Fit_Notes: Fit rises for technically mature BPOs capable of constructing their own tenancy/chargeback model.
criteria_assessments.Implementation_Change_Implication: Design the agent/resource model and cost allocation before scaling programs.
criteria_assessments.Production_Operating_Risk: Commercial attribution and shared-agent economics still need buyer-specific proof.

criteria_assessments.Assessment_Finding: IaC/APIs and repeatable routing patterns can accelerate program launches, but no standardized BPO program-launch SLA or out-of-box tenant factory was established in reviewed evidence.
criteria_assessments.Buyer_Fit_Notes: Fit depends on how well the BPO productizes its own AWS deployment patterns.
criteria_assessments.Implementation_Change_Implication: Buyer should test creation of a new client program from templates under a time target.
criteria_assessments.Production_Operating_Risk: Program cloning can become engineering work if each client has bespoke resources/integrations.

criteria_assessments.Assessment_Finding: Routing/resource access can be segmented, but analytics TBAC has documented gaps and BPO-specific WEM separation is not fully proven.
criteria_assessments.Buyer_Fit_Notes: Fit remains conditional for multi-client operations.
criteria_assessments.Implementation_Change_Implication: Client-specific report/WEM permissions and shared-agent behavior require proof.
criteria_assessments.Production_Operating_Risk: Cross-client reporting access or workforce rule bleed is unacceptable in many outsourcer models.

criteria_assessments.Assessment_Finding: Reviewed public evidence does not establish a standardized per-client usage attribution/chargeback construct covering all Connect and dependent AWS services.
criteria_assessments.Buyer_Fit_Notes: Unknown is not weak; it is a proof requirement before BPO economic fit is accepted.
criteria_assessments.Implementation_Change_Implication: Buyer must demonstrate CUR/tagging/usage allocation across shared and client-specific resources.
criteria_assessments.Production_Operating_Risk: Without accurate attribution, BPO margin and client billing can be distorted.

criteria_assessments.Assessment_Finding: Shared-instance patterns are documented, but cross-client blast-radius behavior across routing, quotas, Lambda, streams and integrations has not been production-proven in reviewed evidence.
criteria_assessments.Buyer_Fit_Notes: No BPO resilience credit until the actual tenancy pattern is proven.
criteria_assessments.Implementation_Change_Implication: Failure isolation must be tested under load with one client's dependency/traffic intentionally degraded.
criteria_assessments.Production_Operating_Risk: A noisy or broken client dependency could affect shared resources or operations.

criteria_assessments.Assessment_Finding: Usage pricing and no-seat baseline can support variable client economics, but shared AWS-service and support allocation plus private discounts remain BPO-specific.
criteria_assessments.Buyer_Fit_Notes: Potential fit-up for variable BPO demand after attribution proof.
criteria_assessments.Implementation_Change_Implication: Contract and internal chargeback model must align to program ramps/contractions.
criteria_assessments.Production_Operating_Risk: Commercial flexibility can be strong while margin attribution remains complex.

criteria_assessments.Assessment_Finding: Five causal break types have been identified around regional capability, implementation engineering, usage economics, AWS operating ownership and strategic AWS coupling.
criteria_assessments.Buyer_Fit_Notes: Decision use is buyer-condition specific; no universal ranking is implied.
criteria_assessments.Implementation_Change_Implication: Each break is tied to trigger, mitigation, owner, cost, proof and exit condition.
criteria_assessments.Production_Operating_Risk: Without causal framing, programmability can be misread as either universal strength or universal complexity.

criteria_assessments.Assessment_Finding: Data portability is strong, but custom flows/Lambda/AWS service architecture and product-tier/lifecycle decisions can create strategic switching cost.
criteria_assessments.Buyer_Fit_Notes: Moves down for buyers with strict multi-cloud portability or low proprietary-cloud coupling tolerance.
criteria_assessments.Implementation_Change_Implication: Require exportable configs/data, IaC/source ownership and exit testing for custom architecture.
criteria_assessments.Production_Operating_Risk: An open data path does not guarantee low application/logic portability.

criteria_assessments.Assessment_Finding: Fit rises with AWS maturity, variable demand, API/IaC culture, data/AI ambition and supported resiliency geography; it falls with weak cloud ownership, strict unsupported sovereignty or no tolerance for multi-service architecture.
criteria_assessments.Buyer_Fit_Notes: Amazon should not be framed as 'builder-only' or 'best for everyone'; fit follows operating model and architecture.
criteria_assessments.Implementation_Change_Implication: Use Fit Sensitivity rather than universal segment labels.
criteria_assessments.Production_Operating_Risk: These conditions materially change buyer outcomes without changing the product itself.

criteria_assessments.Assessment_Finding: Material uncertainties are directly testable: resilience, quotas, AI actions, model behavior, WFM, QA, BPO isolation, integration failure and full TCO.
criteria_assessments.Buyer_Fit_Notes: Proof raises evidence confidence rather than capability score.
criteria_assessments.Implementation_Change_Implication: Buyer-controlled failure/load/change tests are mandatory for high-consequence claims.
criteria_assessments.Production_Operating_Risk: Demo evidence alone would overstate production certainty for a programmable architecture.

criteria_assessments.Assessment_Finding: Contracts/SOWs must explicitly allocate AWS support tier, third-party service dependencies, quotas, data/telecom, AI/model geography, IaC/source ownership and acceptance tests.
criteria_assessments.Buyer_Fit_Notes: Contract discipline is essential for complex regulated/multi-service deployments.
criteria_assessments.Implementation_Change_Implication: Translate architecture into enforceable RACI, acceptance, pricing and exit commitments.
criteria_assessments.Production_Operating_Risk: Shared responsibility makes undocumented assumptions especially costly.

criteria_assessments.Assessment_Finding: Current research uses predominantly primary AWS documentation and explicitly isolates preview, unverified BPO mechanics and Tier 3 practitioner signals.
criteria_assessments.Buyer_Fit_Notes: Evidence quality is high for documented features; unresolved operating claims remain appropriately unverified.
criteria_assessments.Implementation_Change_Implication: Event-driven refresh is required alongside periodic validation.
criteria_assessments.Production_Operating_Risk: AWS changes quickly; pricing, models, Regions, quotas and feature status can stale faster than static market matrices.

criteria_assessments.Assessment_Finding: AWS explicitly exposes service quotas/API throttles and recommends pre-launch sizing, quota-increase requests and production monitoring; many limits are adjustable rather than inherent ceilings.
criteria_assessments.Buyer_Fit_Notes: Fit is strong for buyers with mature capacity governance; risk rises where cloud operations are weak or a hard/non-adjustable quota conflicts with demand.
criteria_assessments.Implementation_Change_Implication: CloudOps capacity planning, alarms, support escalation and load testing are explicit implementation/run-state work.
criteria_assessments.Production_Operating_Risk: Peak/burst workloads can throttle or fail if quotas are not raised in time or monitored with sufficient headroom.

breaks.Affected_Buyer_or_Use_Case: Sovereignty-constrained, multinational or mission-critical buyers with non-negotiable geography/RTO requirements
breaks.Break_Summary: The required geography, resilience or AI-sovereignty architecture cannot be achieved within the supported Connect Customer Region topology or inference path.
breaks.Build_or_Config_Implication: Region, telephony, data, AI and dependency architecture must be explicitly mapped and tested.
breaks.Buyer_Question: Show the exact Region, failover pair, AI inference Region, telecom geography and data path for every critical workload.
breaks.Change_Consequence: Region/model/service changes require architecture revalidation and regression testing.
breaks.Cost_Consequence: Potential duplicate regional resources, additional data/integration engineering, carrier cost and governance overhead.
breaks.Day2_Consequence: Operating teams must monitor paired Regions, dependencies and inference/data-location assumptions.
breaks.Day2_Owner: Cloud Platform Owner / Contact Center Operations
breaks.Exit_Point: Eliminate the proposed architecture if a non-negotiable residency, Region-pair, telephony or recovery requirement cannot be met without unacceptable workaround.
breaks.Mitigation_Method: Choose a supported Region pair; separate workloads; constrain managed AI use; use buyer-approved model/prompt paths; redesign voice/dependency architecture; or select an alternate platform for the affected workload.
breaks.Refresh_Trigger: Region-pair expansion, AI inference-region changes, telephony coverage or compliance-scope changes.
breaks.Trigger_Condition: The buyer requires an unsupported active-active Region pair, strict in-Region AI inference/model behavior, or a voice/feature geography that the exact design cannot provide.

breaks.Affected_Buyer_or_Use_Case: Large enterprise, BPO, regulated or multi-region transformation
breaks.Break_Summary: A technically capable Connect Customer design can become a high- or transformational-gravity cloud program when it combines custom flows, Lambda/API integrations, IAM, Kinesis/data, agentic AI, multi-region resilience and migration under an aggressive timeline.
breaks.Build_or_Config_Implication: Architecture, IAM, quotas, flows, integrations, data, AI, resiliency, testing and cutover work must be decomposed into owned workstreams.
breaks.Buyer_Question: Separate what is native configuration from custom flow, Lambda, API, data-pipeline, AI-tool and multi-region engineering in the proposed design.
breaks.Change_Consequence: Every custom AWS dependency adds regression, support and lifecycle responsibility.
breaks.Cost_Consequence: Cloud engineering, SI, migration, test automation and internal program labor can materially exceed platform activation cost.
breaks.Day2_Consequence: Custom assets, quotas, AWS service dependencies and observability remain owned after go-live.
breaks.Day2_Owner: Cloud Platform Owner / Technical Admin / DevOps
breaks.Exit_Point: Choose a simpler architecture or another platform if required engineering/implementation capacity cannot fit the buyer's timeline, budget or operating model.
breaks.Mitigation_Method: Use packaged Connect Customer capabilities first; standardize flows/integrations; phase advanced AI/data/resilience; use IaC/test automation; assign experienced AWS/CX delivery ownership.
breaks.Ownership_During_Implementation: Customer cloud/contact-center teams + SI/AWS specialists as required
breaks.Refresh_Trigger: Packaging simplification, IaC parity, managed-integration expansion or deployment-tooling changes.
breaks.Trigger_Condition: The buyer wants a broad enterprise replacement plus material AWS-native customization and assumes pay-as-you-go or 'serverless' means low implementation effort.

breaks.Affected_Buyer_or_Use_Case: High-volume, seasonal, complex-integrated or AI-intensive buyers
breaks.Break_Summary: The solution remains technically viable, but usage-based channels, telecom, outbound attempts, AI/tool calls, dependent AWS services, premium support and engineering labor can create an unattractive risk-adjusted TCO.
breaks.Build_or_Config_Implication: Pricing model must include all AWS services and internal/SI labor, not only Connect channel units.
breaks.Buyer_Question: Price our actual 36-month workload including voice, messaging, email, outbound attempts, Profiles/Tasks, Lambda, Kinesis, storage, Bedrock/AgentCore, support and operating labor.
breaks.Change_Consequence: New AI/integration use cases can shift cost into services outside the apparent CCaaS bill.
breaks.Cost_Consequence: Potentially nonlinear consumption and support/engineering cost; can be favorable or unfavorable depending workload composition.
breaks.Day2_Consequence: Continuous usage attribution, anomaly detection and workload optimization become operating functions.
breaks.Exit_Point: Eliminate or redesign if full three-layer TCO exceeds the buyer threshold after realistic peak demand, support, engineering and exit assumptions.
breaks.Mitigation_Method: Build low/base/high 36-month workload models; instrument cost allocation; use native bundled Customer capabilities before add-on AWS services; set budgets/alerts; negotiate enterprise discounts only after modeling commitment risk.
breaks.Refresh_Trigger: Channel/telephony/AI/support pricing or dependency architecture changes.
breaks.Trigger_Condition: High or volatile contact volumes combine with heavy telephony/outbound, custom Lambda/data pipelines, agentic AI and premium support while FinOps visibility is weak.

breaks.Affected_Buyer_or_Use_Case: Lean IT/contact-center teams or organizations with weak AWS governance
breaks.Break_Summary: Connect Customer becomes a poor operating fit when the buyer requires advanced AWS-native customization but lacks CloudOps/IAM/DevOps/FinOps ownership and expects the contact-center vendor to own the full stack.
breaks.Build_or_Config_Implication: Operating-model design must assign responsibilities across contact-center admin, cloud engineering, security, data, AI and support.
breaks.Buyer_Question: Who owns quotas, IAM, CloudWatch, IaC, Lambda/API code, data streams, AI tools, cost anomalies and AWS Support escalations after go-live?
breaks.Change_Consequence: Advanced change requires cross-functional technical ownership rather than only a contact-center admin.
breaks.Cost_Consequence: Additional internal FTE or managed-service cost; support-plan and partner dependency may rise.
breaks.Day2_Consequence: Quota governance, IAM, incident diagnosis, cost controls and custom service dependencies persist.
breaks.Day2_Owner: Cloud Platform Owner / Technical Admin / FinOps / AI Ops
breaks.Exit_Point: Choose a simpler platform/design or funded managed operating model if the buyer will not staff the required ownership.
breaks.Mitigation_Method: Simplify to packaged capabilities; establish a managed service/SI model; train named AWS/Connect owners; implement quota/cost/incident runbooks and change automation.
breaks.Ownership_During_Implementation: Customer operations + cloud platform + managed partner/SI if used
breaks.Refresh_Trigger: Managed-services availability, admin simplification, support operating model or automation changes.
breaks.Trigger_Condition: The architecture uses custom integrations, streams, AI tools, Global Resiliency and IaC while the customer has no durable AWS platform team or managed-service model.

breaks.Affected_Buyer_or_Use_Case: Enterprises with strict multi-cloud portability, merger/divestiture or future exit requirements
breaks.Break_Summary: A low-coupling or multi-cloud strategy can break when customer logic, integrations, data pipelines, AI tooling and operations become deeply embedded in AWS services even though raw data is exportable.
breaks.Build_or_Config_Implication: Architecture must distinguish data portability from application/configuration/operating portability.
breaks.Buyer_Question: Show how we export and recreate routing, configuration, data, integrations and AI behavior outside AWS, and identify what must be rewritten.
breaks.Change_Consequence: Each new AWS-native dependency should be assessed for business value versus exit/rebuild cost.
breaks.Cost_Consequence: Potential rewrite, migration, retraining and parallel-run cost on exit; lifecycle changes such as tier/feature retirement can add migration work.
breaks.Day2_Consequence: Run-state optimization can increase future switching cost as more logic moves into AWS-native components.
breaks.Exit_Point: Choose another architecture if mandated portability/multi-cloud policy cannot tolerate the dependency level required to achieve the target capability.
breaks.Mitigation_Method: Keep domain logic portable where practical; own source/IaC; minimize unnecessary AWS-service coupling; preserve standard exports; test recreation/exit; contract transition assistance.
breaks.Refresh_Trigger: Export/IaC portability changes, tier retirement, major AWS service dependency changes.
breaks.Trigger_Condition: The business case assumes easy future provider portability while the implementation accumulates Lambda, EventBridge, Kinesis, S3, Bedrock/AgentCore, IAM, CloudFormation and custom flow dependencies.

implementation.AI_Work: Moderate-to-high: knowledge, prompts/models, guardrails, tool permissions, action integrity, evaluations, cross-region inference, cost and AI Ops must be productionized.
implementation.Architecture_Work: High when multi-region, regulated, agentic or data-intensive; supported Region pairs and downstream-service dependencies must be mapped.
implementation.Discovery_Complexity: Moderate-to-high: discovery must resolve product tier, Regions, telecom, routing, integrations, IAM, data, quotas, WFM/QM, AI, support tier, IaC and operating ownership before SOW.
implementation.Estimated_Timeline_Band: CONTEXT-DEPENDENT; basic instances can launch quickly, but no universal enterprise duration is supportable from current evidence.
implementation.External_Services_Dependency: Optional but often material in complex programs: experienced AWS/CX SI, managed service or AWS specialists; customer still owns shared-responsibility and account-level governance.
implementation.Gravity_Rationale: Calibration assessment: Moderate for a bounded deployment using current packaged Connect Customer capabilities; High for integrated enterprise transformation; Transformational when multi-region resilience, heavy custom AWS services, agentic AI, data architecture and major legacy migration are combined.
implementation.Integration_Work: Low-to-moderate for native/managed integration paths; High when AppFlow/EventBridge/Lambda/APIs/custom apps and joint support boundaries dominate.
implementation.Key_Assumptions: Exact scope, custom-service count, Regions, number estate, source-platform complexity, data/AI requirements, compliance and buyer AWS maturity determine gravity.
implementation.Migration_Work: Moderate with repeatable patterns; High where legacy numbers, custom routing, recordings/history, CRM logic and operational processes require rebuild/mapping.
implementation.PMO_Need: High for multi-workstream enterprise transformations; lower for bounded deployments.
implementation.Porting_Cutover: Moderate-to-high for global number migration and multi-region design; exact country/carrier and failover approach matter.
implementation.Routing_IVR_Work: Low-to-moderate for standard queues/flows; High for complex reusable flows, Lambda-backed logic and multi-client patterns.
implementation.Testing_UAT: High in complex programs: native simulation helps, but end-to-end dependency, quota/load, failover, AI-action, WFM/QM, voice and cutover tests remain required.
implementation.Training_Change_Management: Moderate-to-high; agents/supervisors benefit from packaged workspace, while admins, cloud engineers, security, data, FinOps and AI Ops can require new operating processes.

sow_exposure.Acceptance_Criterion: Buyer-scripted active-active/failover test meets RTO/RPO and data/customer-path thresholds.
sow_exposure.Customer_Responsibility: Approve geography, sovereignty and recovery requirements; provide dependent-system owners.
sow_exposure.Required_SOW_Language: Name primary/replica Regions, supported pair, replicated resources, traffic distribution, telephony, external dependencies, data/AI inference locations, RTO/RPO and failover acceptance tests.
sow_exposure.Typical_Assumption_or_Exclusion: Any AWS Region can be paired active-active and external dependencies will fail over automatically.
sow_exposure.Vendor_or_SI_Responsibility: Design/configure supported resiliency architecture and identify non-replicated dependencies.

sow_exposure.Acceptance_Criterion: Peak/load test remains under agreed thresholds with alarms and escalation validated.
sow_exposure.Customer_Responsibility: Provide forecast/contact/agent concurrency and growth profile.
sow_exposure.Required_SOW_Language: Inventory every relevant quota; include target peak, headroom, increase lead time, API throttles, alarms, launch freeze and escalation path.
sow_exposure.Typical_Assumption_or_Exclusion: AWS scale assumed to remove quota planning or API throttling risk.
sow_exposure.Vendor_or_SI_Responsibility: Size/request quotas and implement monitoring/runbooks as scoped.

sow_exposure.Acceptance_Criterion: Buyer admins can perform agreed routine changes; engineered logic passes regression/failure tests.
sow_exposure.Required_SOW_Language: Classify each flow as native configuration, reusable flow logic, Lambda/API/tool call or custom application; name source/IaC owner, test/rollback and support boundaries.
sow_exposure.Typical_Assumption_or_Exclusion: Demo flows assumed to remain no-code and self-managed at any complexity.
sow_exposure.Vendor_or_SI_Responsibility: Build/configure agreed flows and custom services; deliver source/IaC where applicable.

sow_exposure.Acceptance_Criterion: Critical workflows pass normal, auth-expiry, dependency-outage and retry/recovery tests.
sow_exposure.Customer_Responsibility: Provide target-system access, test data and application SMEs.
sow_exposure.Required_SOW_Language: Document AppFlow/EventBridge/Lambda/API/custom-app dependencies, data/actions, auth/IAM, quotas, versioning, telemetry, error handling, retries, support RACI and acceptance tests.
sow_exposure.Typical_Assumption_or_Exclusion: Prebuilt integration assumed to mean one vendor-owned connector with simple incident ownership.
sow_exposure.Vendor_or_SI_Responsibility: Configure supported pattern and disclose customer/SI-owned custom components.

sow_exposure.Acceptance_Criterion: Buyer data appears within required latency and can be reconciled/exported at required scale.
sow_exposure.Required_SOW_Language: Specify data objects, retention, freshness, stream/data-lake path, S3/Kinesis/Firehose resources, encryption, schema ownership, downstream query stack, cost and export/exit needs.
sow_exposure.Typical_Assumption_or_Exclusion: Native data lake or Kinesis assumed to be interchangeable and all long-term data retained automatically.
sow_exposure.Vendor_or_SI_Responsibility: Configure data associations/streams and document customer-owned resources.

sow_exposure.Customer_Responsibility: Provide historical demand, staffing rules, QA gold sets and SMEs.
sow_exposure.Required_SOW_Language: Define history/data minimums, queue/channel mappings, workforce rules, schedule constraints, evaluation rubrics, calibration, dashboards and admin roles.
sow_exposure.Typical_Assumption_or_Exclusion: Included native capability assumed to be immediately accurate/operational.
sow_exposure.Vendor_or_SI_Responsibility: Configure native WFM/QM/analytics and disclose product limits.

sow_exposure.Acceptance_Criterion: Meets buyer grounding, latency, action-integrity, safety, cost and fallback thresholds.
sow_exposure.Customer_Responsibility: Provide knowledge, policies, test corpus, backend sandbox and action approval rules.
sow_exposure.Required_SOW_Language: Name each AI workflow, model resolution/pinning, inference Region, knowledge, prompt version, guardrails, security profile, MCP/tool contracts, human escalation, evaluations, logging, disable/fallback and dependent AWS charges.
sow_exposure.Typical_Assumption_or_Exclusion: Included AI assumed production-ready without model, knowledge, guardrail, tool and cost design.
sow_exposure.Vendor_or_SI_Responsibility: Configure/integrate/tune AI and document managed-vs-pinned model behavior.

sow_exposure.Customer_Responsibility: Provide number inventories, LOAs and regulatory information.
sow_exposure.Required_SOW_Language: Country-by-country number type, porting, outbound reach, CLI, emergency services, recording, telecom fees, carrier path, failover and acceptance tests.
sow_exposure.Typical_Assumption_or_Exclusion: 110+ country coverage assumed to satisfy every buyer number/use case identically.
sow_exposure.Vendor_or_SI_Responsibility: Provision/port supported services and identify unsupported exceptions.

sow_exposure.Acceptance_Criterion: Security architecture passes buyer control mapping; no unsupported dependency remains in regulated path.
sow_exposure.Customer_Responsibility: Approve control requirements and own account/security governance.
sow_exposure.Required_SOW_Language: Define IAM roles/policies, encryption keys, logging, data locations, service-by-service compliance scope, third-party responsibilities and security acceptance evidence.
